cards.explanation: The answer is visions and revelations from the Lord. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says, “…I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.” (2 Corinthians 12:1) He just said there's nothing to gain, and he keeps going anyway. So the next part is all about what the Lord showed him.

The answer is God. Paul, talking about the man caught up to the third heaven, says, “Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.” (2 Corinthians 12:2) I love how honest that is, friends. Paul doesn't pretend to have the answer, and he's fine saying God has it.

The answer is False. Paul says, “The things he heard were inexpressible, things that man is not permitted to tell.” (2 Corinthians 12:4) He heard them in Paradise, but he isn't permitted to pass them on. I'd be bursting at the seams, and Paul just lets it be.

The answer is True. Paul says, “…I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.” (2 Corinthians 12:5) He'll brag about the man caught up to Paradise, but when it's about himself, he points to his weaknesses. That's a backwards kind of bragging, and I love it.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth.” (2 Corinthians 12:6) It's the truth, so it wouldn't make him a fool. Then he holds back anyway, and that takes real strength.

The answer is conceited. Paul says, “So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.” (2 Corinthians 12:7) That's the word he uses. Having a front-row seat to great revelations could go to anybody's head, and I'd be the first one with a crooked hat.

The answer is a thorn in his flesh. Paul says, “…I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.” (2 Corinthians 12:7) He doesn't spell out what the thorn is, so I won't guess either, friends. We know it tormented him, and we know he was given it.

The answer is “My grace is sufficient for you.” The Lord says to Paul, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9) Paul pleaded three times about the thorn, and that's the answer he got. It's not what he asked for, but it's what the Lord said.

The answer is weakness. The Lord says, “…My power is perfected in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9) That's strange to our ears, friends, because we expect power to show up where things are strong. But He says it plain, and Paul takes Him at His word.

The answer is so the power of Christ may rest on him. Paul says, “Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.” (2 Corinthians 12:9) Notice the word gladly. That comes right after the Lord says, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.”

The answer is strong! Paul writes, “For when I am weak, then I am strong.” (2 Corinthians 12:10) It sounds like a riddle, friends. Right before it, the Lord says His power is perfected in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9), and Paul says he'll boast so that the power of Christ may rest on him.
